column2: Circles are divided into 8 stages, with 2 Circles in each stage.\nThe earlier Circle means just entered; the later one means nearly complete.
Senses and emits mana. Produces simple phenomena such as lighting a candle or raising a breeze.
Holds mana in a steady form and controls it precisely. Mana shields, small projectiles, bodywork support.
Wields complete magic that can be used independently in real combat. Full-fledged attack magic such as fireballs and ice lances.
Chains several spells together or affects a wide area. Compound magic, area attacks, powerful barriers.
Wields magic refined and powerful enough to change the course of a battlefield. Large-scale environmental interference, advanced applications.
Deeply interferes with the fundamental workings of reality, such as space, climate and life. A strategic asset on the scale of a nation.
Completes a unique magic system and produces phenomena beyond the limits of existing magic, such as deploying a domain or directly interfering with a gate's structure.
A realm not established by the magical theory of the present age.

Magic is classified into six schools. Anyone can learn all six without distinction, but most study one or two in depth. The Dark school is not forbidden but a controlled discipline, taught on a limited basis even at the Academy.
The school that handles natural objects and phenomena with mana. It borrows the elements and energies that make up the world to produce power.
The school that purifies harmful influences and grants blessings and protection. Faith is not required.
The school that gnaws at a target's existence and will with traces of death and negative states. It wields the power of curses and decay.
The school that directly intervenes in the bodies and life processes of living things. It manipulates the biological functions of a target's body.
The school that produces phenomena with pure mana alone. All mana use that belongs to no other school falls here.
The school that infuses mana into bodies, weapons and equipment to raise their physical performance. It pushes past the limits of body and tools.
The Office and five wings. Press to see the facilities.
The administrative body that runs the whole Academy.
The wing where classes and official events are held.
Hosts lectures common to the whole Academy and seats several hundred.
Official events such as entrance and graduation ceremonies are held here.
The exteriors of the twelve halls are identical to their interiors in structure and are distinguished only by each faculty's symbol color and emblem.
Each hall has its own lecture rooms, professors' studies, a small library, practice space and a lounge.
A complex of several buildings with courtyards and gardens.
Bedroom, desk, wardrobe and a small private bathroom.
Lounges, reception rooms, shared study rooms, laundry and bathing facilities.
With permission, anyone may enter another's room regardless of gender; entering without permission is strictly forbidden.
A street-centered wing for meals, shopping and rest.
Training facilities for preparing gate subjugation.
Recreates forests, snowfields, ruins, caves and more to practice dealing with monsters, tactics and teamwork.
The wing where banquets and socializing take place.
A small city-state at the center of the continent and an internationally neutral nation. It formed around the Academy, and its independence and neutrality are guaranteed by international treaty.
The strongest power on the continent. Great nobles and lords share power around the imperial family.
A traditional kingdom with a clear hierarchy of royalty and old nobility. It values honor, chivalry and succession.
A kingdom that built its wealth on trade, finance and the alchemy industry. Merchant families earned titles and became nobles.
A nation that serves Aurelia, goddess of abundance, life and order, as its sole patron deity. It is governed by written law.
The ancient homeland of the elves. Ancient forests, nature magic and spirit arts flourish there, and it is ruled by the elven Council of Elders.
Entrance ceremony on March 1 · Orientation week March 1–7
Grand Hall · Faculty Halls · Dormitory Wing
Parties may set out early from March 2 · Subjugation commissions posted March 8 · Monthly subjugation duty begins on the 8th
The entrance ceremony is held in the Grand Hall on March 1, and the Chancellor welcomes the new students. They receive their faculty's brooch and are guided to their faculty hall.
March 1 through 7 is orientation week, with tours of the faculty halls, moving into the dormitory, meeting classmates and an introduction to the facilities.
Subjugation commissions are posted from the 8th, and students who wish may form parties and set out early from the 2nd. The once-a-month subjugation duty begins on the 8th.
Anyone regardless of faculty (students who stayed at the Academy during winter break)
A New Year banquet held for one day on January 1. A light social gathering held in the Small Banquet Hall in the evening.
Students who stayed at the Academy over winter break gather casually, and there are no restrictions on dress or seating. Refreshments and music are provided, and there is no merit.
Anyone may attend regardless of faculty, so it is a good chance to get closer to classmates you have never spoken with.
Students (enter with a chosen partner; attending without a partner is also allowed)
Seats of honor for the top 3 faculties · lowest seats for the bottom 3
A spring ball held for one evening on April 20. Held in the Grand Banquet Hall, where students choose a partner, enter together and dance. Attending without a partner is fine too.
The top 3 faculties sit in the seats of honor and the bottom 3 in the lowest seats.

During the ball, couples can slip out to the terrace and garden for time alone, and students of lower faculties may enter only if invited as a companion by a student of a higher faculty. There is no merit.
Several gates of grade A or above chosen by the Office (simultaneous subjugation)
All students (must take part by forming a party)
Calculated by the same rules as regular subjugations
A large-scale five-day subjugation held June 10 to 14 and November 10 to 14. The Office picks several gates of grade A or above and subjugates them simultaneously.

Every student must form a party and take part. After the commission is posted, parties form, set out by carriage, and report to the Office on return. Merit is calculated by the same rules as regular subjugations.
Classes are suspended during the event, and the most parties of the year are on the move.
Parties enter the same mock gate and compete on the time taken to subjugate it (instructors record and judge)
March D · April C · May C · September B · December A
All participating students receive half the base merit of that grade · the top 3 teams get an extra 20, 10 and 5
Only the faculty of the first-place team receives it

Held for one day on March, April, May, September and December 15. Each party enters the same mock gate in the Training Wing's mock zone and competes on the time taken to subjugate it, while instructors keep time and judge.
The mock gate grade rises over the months: D in March, C in April and May, B in September, A in December.

Participating students receive half the base merit of that grade as personal merit, and the top 3 teams receive an extra 20, 10 and 5 merit. Faculty merit goes only to the faculty of the first-place team.
One-on-one or in teams (sign up on the spot that day)

Held for one day on the 25th of March through June and September through December. Students test their skill one-on-one or in teams at the Training Wing dueling ground, and sign-up is taken on the spot that day.

Students use real weapons, but the dueling ground's damage-reversal ward prevents fatal injury: mana is spent instead of wounds, and whoever fills the ward's limit first loses. Instructors preside and judge.
There is no merit; it is a chance for students to show their own skill.
July 30 (first semester settlement) · December 30 (second semester settlement · closing ball)
Awards ceremony in the Grand Hall by day · banquet in the Grand Banquet Hall in the evening
Final announcement of faculty merit rankings · award for first place in personal merit
Merit resets, break starts the next day

The first semester settlement is held on July 30 and the second on December 30, each for one day. By day an awards ceremony in the Grand Hall announces the final faculty merit rankings and honors the first-place student in personal merit.
In the evening a banquet follows in the Grand Banquet Hall; in December it is called the closing ball, and students dance with their partners.
After the awards, merit resets and break begins the next day.
Stay at the Academy or return home · Living Wing stays open · no classes
No monthly duty, voluntary participation · gates still appear during break
Merit earned during break counts toward the next semester
A summer break running from July 31 to August 31. It begins the day after the first semester settlement and ends when the second semester starts on September 1.
Students may stay at the Academy or return home; the Living Wing keeps operating and there are no classes. There is no monthly subjugation duty, and participation is voluntary.
Gates appear during break too, so subjugation continues, and merit earned during break counts toward the next semester. The Mock Raid and Friendly Duel are not held.
December 31 – end of February (classes and entrance ceremony on March 1)
New Year Banquet in the Small Banquet Hall on January 1 · Mock Raid and Friendly Duel not held

A winter break running from December 31 to the end of the following February. It begins the day after the second semester settlement and ends with the start of classes and the entrance ceremony on March 1.

Gates appear during break too, and merit earned during break counts toward the next semester. On January 1 a New Year banquet is held in the Small Banquet Hall. The Mock Raid and Friendly Duel are not held.
The twelve faculties are split into two factions of six, Legacy Society and Pioneer Society, and each faction's faculty representatives clear the same mock gate in their own way
Instructors record time taken and damage to judge the winner
The six faculties of the winning faction receive 30 faculty merit
Legacy Society sun flag · Pioneer Society moon flag

A large-scale faculty contest held for three days, October 20 to 22. The twelve faculties are split into two factions of six, the Legacy Society and the Pioneer Society, and each faction chooses faculty representatives to clear the same mock gate in their own way.

The Legacy Society uses proven formations and traditional tactics, while the Pioneer Society uses new magic and tactics. Instructors record time taken and damage to judge the winner, and the six faculties of the winning faction receive 30 faculty merit.
The Legacy Society flies the sun flag and the Pioneer Society the moon flag.
No classes. All time apart from meals is free time.
Wake up and breakfast (skipping meals allowed)
